what_it_involves: A yearly balance of the protein people eat, by food, source and origin (production, imports, exports), with a memo line for the imported feed behind domestic meat, eggs, milk and farmed fish; aligned with the FAO food balance sheet and the EU balance-sheet method
lead_actors: MAE; NSO; MOH (National Institute of Nutrition)
evidence_basis: Every tracked foreign target has a statistic; the two largest levers in the balance model are unmeasured
status_v0_8: active (reworded in v0.8 for the human-food focus)

what_it_involves: Amino acids, low-protein diets, precision feeding, by-product meals and FCR benchmarking; target soybean-meal inclusion falling 1 to 2% a year (relative)
evidence_basis: Cuts 2050 soybean-meal need by about 3.4 Mt in the model; China achieved a comparable pace
status_v0_8: retired in v0.8: feed output, outside the human-food focus (kept as the v0.7 record)

what_it_involves: A defined new-food procedure with statutory timelines and reliance on reference regulators; for cultivated food, a safety lane that relies on the FAO and WHO 2023 hazard framework for cell-based food and on Singapore Food Agency approvals
trigger_or_signpost: Food Safety Law and decree (2026 to 2027)
evidence_basis: Needed to import as well as to make; Korea amended a rule in about nine months; FAO and WHO (2023) set out eight hazard categories for cell-based food across four production stages, most already known from conventional food
status_v0_8: active (reworded in v0.8 for the human-food focus); v0.10: reliance basis for a cultivated-food safety lane named (wave 13, L3)

what_it_involves: 10,000 to 30,000 L of open, food-grade pilot fermentation, with sensory and food-safety testing for the products made on it
lead_actors: MOST; Ho Chi Minh City; universities; DFIs
evidence_basis: Rivals put pilot capacity in designated zones (EECi, ScaleUp Bio, BioE3 hubs)
status_v0_8: active (reworded in v0.8 for the human-food focus)

move: Protein-quality laboratory and open price series
what_it_involves: Accredited testing for protein quality, authenticity and contaminants; a public price and cost series for food protein ingredients, including domestic soybean and mung bean farm-gate prices and imported food-bean unit values by origin
evidence_basis: Imports and domestic products need the same checks; adulteration is a listed wildcard; v0.1 found no Vietnamese lab offering amino-acid digestibility tests; the EU legume roadmap proposes a legumes observatory of prices and volumes, and a bean price series would close OQ-094
status_v0_8: active (reworded in v0.8 for the human-food focus); v0.10: domestic bean prices and imported food-bean unit values added to the price series (wave 13, L7)

move: Residue-carbon rules and a by-product atlas
what_it_involves: Mapped volumes of cassava pulp, straw, stillage, okara and brewery streams; collection contracts; food-safety rules for food-grade side streams
evidence_basis: Straw must be 100% collected on 1 million ha by 2030; EU feed law bans some waste streams
status_v0_8: active (reworded in v0.8 for the human-food focus)

what_it_involves: Qualify algal and oilseed omega-3 oils in shrimp and marine-fish feeds; track EPA plus DHA needs
evidence_basis: Omega-3 is a tighter constraint than protein; alternatives are commercial
status_v0_8: retired in v0.8: feed output, outside the human-food focus (kept as the v0.7 record)

what_it_involves: Raised sites, surface water rather than groundwater, and process designs for 40 degC cooling water in the Mekong
evidence_basis: Subsidence about 1.1 cm a year; plants built after 2035 in coastal Ca Mau or Vinh Long face flood risk in their lifetime
status_v0_8: active

what_it_involves: Two tracks and a product component. (a) Senior engineers: a biotechnology plus food process engineering talent master's under Decision 1002, proposed through MOET's annual talent-programme cycle (Official Letter 5695/BGDĐT-GDĐH, 17 September 2025), with a pilot-scale capstone co-taught by industry on the shared pilot line once it exists (RM-04, T5). (b) Operators: MOIT food colleges and FIRI, with hands-on time on the tanks of tolling hosts. (c) A buyer-set product challenge lab: a one-semester, credit-bearing product-design course at one or two food-technology faculties on problems set and part-funded by Vietnamese buyers (T1, T9, T10 products), shown at the FID student contest. Industry placements and links to foreign plants
trigger_or_signpost: None needed to start; hands-on modules need tolling-host tanks or sites abroad until shared pilot capacity (RM-04) exists by 2030
evidence_basis: Senior process talent is the named bottleneck; biotech graduate targets exist; Decision 1002 has no operator component; no fermentation short course for industry and no alternative-protein course found; course fees are small (20 engineers at USD 3,100 each is about USD 62,000, travel excluded; our calculation) but hands-on training needs pilot-scale kit; Berkeley runs a bioprocess capstone at a 300 L pilot unit and ran industry-set product challenge labs (about 32 students a semester, at least three startups); the FID contest drew 144 projects in 2025
source_ids: ECF-41; ECF-39; SLW-07; SLW-08; SLW-09; SLW-14; SLW-17; SLW-20; VCO-21; AML-21; AML-22; AML-32; AML-33
status_v0_8: active; v0.10: split into senior-engineer and operator tracks, MOIT added as lead actor, pilot-kit constraint added; teaching capstone (L8) and buyer-set product challenge lab (AML-C1) folded in as components (wave 13, L6 and L8)

what_it_involves: Name food-fermentation sites in the MAE biotechnology-cluster plan (due December 2026) and provincial hi-tech agriculture zones: Ho Chi Minh City with Dong Nai, Tay Ninh, the Mekong river belt, the Mekong shrimp coast
evidence_basis: The bioeconomy map is still blank; provinces can now create hi-tech agriculture zones
status_v0_8: active (reworded in v0.8 for the human-food focus)

what_it_involves: USD 5 to 15 M a year for food-protein innovation, reviewed each five-year plan
evidence_basis: Peer budgets: Denmark about USD 12 M, Germany about EUR 6 M, Canada about USD 22 M a year. Scale check: USD 5 to 15 M a year is VND 130 to 390 billion at 26,000 VND per USD, about 47% to 140% of all NAFOSTED approvals for new projects in 2023 (VND 278.3 billion, all fields) or 70% to 210% of its 2023 disbursements (VND 185.5 billion) (our calculation). A first step at NAFOSTED scale is one directed call of about VND 9 to 10 billion: 10 ordinary or 3 strong-group projects (our calculation)
status_v0_8: active (reworded in v0.8 for the human-food focus); v0.10: NAFOSTED scale check and a first directed call added (wave 13, L6)

move: Concessional finance window for first plants
what_it_involves: DFI co-finance and guarantees with a named food-manufacturer offtake (our suggestion), for first plants at T4 and T5 scale; ready to open when a signpost trips. A T1-scale line (USD 0.28 to 1.38 M installed) can draw on existing instruments: SME credit guarantees and finance leases, probably SME Development Fund loans, and possibly Decree 57/2018 processing support
evidence_basis: Cutting the capital charge from 12% to 9% does as much as the cost learning expected by 2030; the Ho Chi Minh City SME credit guarantee fund caps guarantees at about USD 1.3 M per customer for investment loans (our calculation), enough for a T1 line but not for a fermentation first plant
status_v0_8: active (reworded in v0.8 for the human-food focus); v0.10: narrowed to T4 and T5 scale; T1 uses existing instruments (wave 13, L5); retired insect source ECO-01 dropped from source_ids

move: Join regional approval and statistics networks
what_it_involves: Take part in any ASEAN reliance work and in the EU-style balance-sheet method
evidence_basis: Reliance is how smaller regulators keep pace; the leading EU NGO soy-dependency analysis (The Protein Project, 2026) builds on the same FAOSTAT food balance sheet protein matrix as the study, so neither RM-01 nor RM-13 needs a change of method
status_v0_8: active; v0.10: method check against the EU soy-dependency analysis added (wave 13, L7)

move: Seed research on cultivated seafood cells and gas fermentation
what_it_involves: Small programmes with foreign partners on Vietnamese species and on gas-fermentation strains. Proposed species: Asian seabass and grouper, which have food-oriented muscle cell lines abroad (Thiruvalluvar University, India; Pukyong National University, Korea; James Cook University), with striped catfish as a low-cost model species. Component: open flavour and off-flavour profiles of cooked tra catfish, tilapia, carp and pond loach (GC-MS and GC-O with a trained panel), published for makers of plant-based, hybrid and cultivated seafood
evidence_basis: Vietnam has 2 of 494 gas-fermentation papers and 1 cultivated-meat paper; food-oriented muscle lines exist for grouper (2024) and Asian seabass (2025), read as metadata only (Low); catfish lines are virology lines; Coefficient Giving's 2026 taste call names carp, tilapia, milkfish, catfish and pond loach and asks for open flavour data; Vietnamese groups already study pangasius flavour and tilapia off-flavour
source_ids: FTG-14; HSC-01; SLS-13; SLS-14; SLS-15; SLS-16; SCI-10; CGG-03; CAP-57; CGG-15; CGG-16
status_v0_8: active; v0.10: proposed species (L4, Low) and open fish flavour profiles (CGG-C1, L9) added as components (wave 13)

move: Clear rules for second-hand fermentation equipment
what_it_involves: Customs and tax treatment and a register of available used tanks for 2027 to 2030
evidence_basis: Meati assets sold for USD 75,000 against a USD 15 to 20 M valuation; the one ethanol-plant retrofit GFI cites (Superbrewed Food) was paused in 2024 and first output moved to a contract manufacturer, which favours used equipment and contract capacity over domestic retrofits
status_v0_8: active; v0.10: Superbrewed retrofit precedent added (wave 13, L2)

what_it_involves: Plants beyond about 1% of high-protein feed protein
trigger_or_signpost: SP-01 sustained and pilot cost within 1.2 times fishmeal-protein parity
evidence_basis: No national feed system has reached 1% novel protein
status_v0_8: retired in v0.8: feed output, outside the human-food focus (kept as the v0.7 record)

move: Power-to-protein demonstration on the Mekong shrimp coast
what_it_involves: A demonstration plant co-located with a hydrogen project and aquafeed buyers
trigger_or_signpost: Delivered green hydrogen below USD 2 per kg; firm renewable power below USD 45 per MWh
evidence_basis: Five conditions in chapter 21; no Vietnamese research base yet
status_v0_8: retired in v0.8: feed output, outside the human-food focus (kept as the v0.7 record)

what_it_involves: A GMP plant making high-value proteins for regional brands
trigger_or_signpost: New-food route, SP-12 or SP-13, and an anchor customer
evidence_basis: Works today only for high-value proteins
status_v0_8: active

what_it_involves: A first plant supplying sugar to fermenters
trigger_or_signpost: An Asian straw plant above 80% of design capacity for a full year
evidence_basis: Every Western commercial plant has shut; Panipat reached 62%
status_v0_8: active

what_it_involves: Multi-origin contracts, formulation flexibility and working stocks of soybean meal and fishmeal sized to recent shocks
pays_off_in: C; D (protects A and B against later shocks)
evidence_basis: The 2026 Middle East conflict helped raise feed prices 10 to 14% between January and April 2026
status_v0_8: retired in v0.8: feed output, outside the human-food focus (kept as the v0.7 record)

move: Import monitoring and equal standards for protein imports
what_it_involves: Track volumes and unit values of plant, microbial and fermented protein-ingredient imports for food, and of soybean imports (HS 1201, which carry food soybeans) with their origin concentration; apply the same food-safety and quality rules to imports and domestic products
evidence_basis: No baseline series for these imports exists; soybean imports came 89% from Brazil and the United States in 2025 (our calculation from customs shares of 45.8% and 43.6%); the 1973 US soybean export embargo is the precedent for an origin shock
status_v0_8: active (reworded in v0.8 for the human-food focus); v0.10: soybean imports and origin concentration added to the monitoring list (wave 13, L7)
